text:
mike: Quick update — I ran a microbatch sweep comparing streaming chat vs non-streaming completions on the g5 nodes this morning. Wanted to share numbers and a few suspicious kernel picks.

sara: awesome, drop the TL;DR first pls — p95/p99 tradeoffs? :eyes:

mike: TL;DR: for short-turn chats (avg len ~80 tokens) MB=4 gives best p95 with streaming enabled, MB=12 maximizes throughput for non-streaming but p99 jumps ~2.3x. KV cache hit behavior explains most of the gap.

kai: can you paste the perf run command you used?

mike: sure — used our bench harness with realistic prefix distribution:
```
./bench --model /models/romulus-7b --profile streaming,completions --mb-sweep 1,2,4,8,12,16 --seq 256 --workers 64 --warm 120s
```
Outputs: p50/p95/p99 and tokens/s per run.

ben: did you force kernel selection or let the runtime pick? we've seen suboptimal kernels for small sequence lengths.

mike: let runtime auto-select. Noticed the runtime chose int8-kernel-v2 for MB<=4 and fp16-kernel for MB>=8 on A100s. Profiling shows kernel-v2 has lower per-token latency but worse tail when KV cache misses happen.

perf-bot: profiling dump attached (summary): avg kernel time (mb=4, stream)=8.6ms, tail spikes to 40-90ms on KV misses; mb=12 non-stream avg=11.2ms, tail 18-25ms. KV hit-rate: 0.78 (mb=4, stream) vs 0.95 (mb=12 non-stream).

sara: that hit-rate delta is large. why is streaming MB=4 suffering KV misses more? I thought streaming preserves KV across turns the same as completions.

mike: two reasons: (1) streaming chat workload had higher session churn in the sim (short sessions with many small prompts) so we ended up evicting prefix caches more frequently; (2) our current KV cache sharding is keyed to request batch id which fragments better for higher MB sizes.

kai: ah — so cache fragmentation + smaller MB sizes => more distinct cache entries and less reuse. Did you capture eviction counts?

mike: yep. eviction_count per second: MB=4 stream = 230 eps, MB=12 non-stream = 42 eps. Memory footprint for cached KV also shows more small allocations causing allocator pressure and occasional GC pauses (~10-30ms) which align with p99 spikes.

ben: interesting. So the latency SLO vs throughput tradeoff isn't just kernel or batching — allocator and cache topology matter too. Any quick mitigation ideas?

mike: a few proposals we tried locally:
- increase per-worker KV capacity for streaming workers (reduce evictions)
- merge small KV shards for chat routing to improve reuse
- change kernel selection rule to prefer the slightly slower but more stable kernel for streaming path (reduces p99 spikes)

sara: do you have numbers for those mitigations? even a small p99 improvement helps.

mike: short results from the canary runs:
- +kv-capacity: p95 improved 6-8%, p99 down 28% (MB=4, stream)
- merged shards: p99 down 34%, avg latency unchanged
- kernel override (force fp16-stable): p95 +2% worse, p99 down 45%

kai: kernel override hurting p95 but massively improving p99 — that's actually a good trade for us since SLO is p99=200ms. What about throughput loss for completions if we force fp16-stable globally?

mike: global override reduces tokens/s by ~12% at MB=12. But we can do a routing policy: streaming endpoints prefer stable kernel, completions endpoints keep auto. That isolates the cost.

ben: any regressions surfaced by the profiling that we should file?

mike: yes — two small ones:
1) allocator path: small-object allocator has an O(n) scan when a free list gets fragmented; reproducer attached. That turned up as GC pauses when eviction churn was high.
2) kernel selection heuristic: it prioritizes raw throughput score but doesn't consider cache miss sensitivity. We should weight kernel score by observed KV-miss tail penalty.

sara: can you attach the reproducer and a short runbook for eng-infra to triage?

mike: attached gist links in thread (copied below). Example repro command for allocator issue:
```
# spin 1000 short chat sessions to stress small allocs
./bench --sessions 1000 --avg-turn 3 --seq 64 --mb 4 --duration 300
```
Collectors: perf -> flamegraphs, heapdump at 60s.

perf-bot: flamegraph links:
- https://internal.perf/fg/1829001234/mb4_stream.svg
- https://internal.perf/fg/1829001240/mb12_nonstream.svg

mike: proposal for next steps:
1) patch allocator to avoid O(n) scans (low risk)
2) add a kernel scoring metric that adds a "tail-sensitivity" penalty when KV miss rate > threshold
3) add per-endpoint routing override (streaming -> stable kernel) in config
4) run a 24h MB-sweep on canary pool to validate (capture p50/p95/p99 + eviction rates)

ben: +1 for all. do we need product sign-off for changing kernel routing on streaming endpoints?

sara: product ok as long as we keep the default for existing customers and only change routing for the new streaming tier. also need to note cost delta for dedicated customers.

kai: I'll pick up allocator repro and start a branch for kernel scoring. mike, can you open the perf ticket with attachments?

mike: done — ticket INF-4821 with runs + flamegraphs + repro steps. linking here: https://redwood.internal/inf/4821

deploy-bot: canary job queued: canary-mb-sweep-182900 — will run on night window 02:00-06:00 UTC.

sara: thanks team. let's sync on results tomorrow after the overnight run. :thumbsup:

mike: added a short note to the ops-runbook: if p99 > 250ms after change -> rollback kernel override and increase KV capacity.

ben: good. one final ask — can we add a small metric to the dashboard: eviction_rate and kernel_choice per endpoint? would help correlate regressions.

mike: yep will open dashboard PR after canary results.

kai: nice work.
